name: theme-library-reach-syntax
body:
source: change request "let theme CSS reference any file in the template library" — theme CSS should reach any library file (shared `media/`, stylesheets, other themes' files) for both `url()` and `@import`.

Decision [autonomous]: extend the existing prefix vocabulary rather than introduce a single library-root prefix. Two reserved prefixes, both valid for `url()` and `@import`:
- `media:` (kept) — the canonical internal/template.MediaURLPrefix() token, the single source of truth read by the step-6 scanner, the serve-time rewriteThemeCSS and the agent-guide drift test. It stays relative to the library's `media/` and gains `@import` support (previously an explicit error). Replacing it with a library-root prefix would be a breaking rename of a shipped, documented, drift-tested token.
- `theme:<name>/` (new) — maps onto the server's existing ThemesPath route (/assets/templates/themes/<name>/) exactly as `media:` maps onto MediaPath; gives a natural unknown-theme error and a confinement boundary.

Rationale for rejecting the single library-root prefix: the server already serves two distinct asset roots (media/ and themes/<name>/) through separate routes; one library-root prefix would either reproduce a media-vs-themes dispatcher behind a new token (no gain) or expose non-servable library entries (slides/, sections/, library.yaml, AGENTS.md). The guard set is retained — no absolute paths, no `..` escape, no reference outside the library, any scheme rejected, `@import` bounded and cycle-safe across the whole import graph, file:line errors — with `..` confined per tree.

Consequence for the code (for the plan-writer): MediaURLPrefix stays the media token; a `theme:` token is added in the same single-source-of-truth pattern; the step-6 scanner follows cross-tree imports (same theme, another theme, media/) with a graph-wide visiting set; the serve-time rewrite gains the `theme:` mapping and must also rewrite `.css` served from the `media/` route, so an imported media stylesheet's own references are rewritten. No planned Implementation nodes are authored here.
